title: Operational service contracts and capacity roadmap
author: Marco Hernandez
body:
Overview

This document defines the next 12–18 month operational roadmap for service-level contracts (SLCs) and capacity planning across the Redwood inference platform. It sets concrete SLO targets, capacity assumptions, and rollout phases for Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to align product, SRE, and platform engineering on predictable economics, clear owners, and an executable migration path for high-volume customers.

Audience
- Platform engineering and SRE
- Product managers for Redwood API and Dedicated
- Solutions engineering and customer success

Goals (measurable)
- Define and publish standard SLC templates for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private by Q1 2026.
- Achieve 99.9% availability for Hosted inference endpoints and 99.95% for Dedicated pools (monthly) by Q3 2026.
- Implement capacity-driven billing telemetry to within 5% accuracy of true GPU utilization by Q2 2026.
- Reduce cost-per-token for median generation workloads by 18% via batching and quantization profiles by Q4 2026.

Service contracts and standard SLOs
- Hosted API (public tenants):
  - Availability: 99.9% (monthly uptime), exclude scheduled maintenance windows (48h notice).
  - Latency: p95 <= 120ms for short generation requests (<=128 tokens); p95 <= 650ms for up-to-512 tokens.
  - Error budget: 0.1% per month.
  - Throttling policy: soft quotas with 429 responses when sustained > 2x baseline QPS for 2 minutes.
- Dedicated (reserved pools):
  - Availability: 99.95% (monthly) for configured capacity.
  - Latency: p95 <= 80ms for <=128 token requests using pinned model variants.
  - Capacity guarantee: baseline throughput commitments documented in the contract (GPU slot count + burst policy).
- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Availability SLA is negotiated per-customer; default operational playbook assumes 99.5% unless additional SLAs purchased.
  - Support windows and on-call escalation differ; see Customer Private Deployment Guide link in Related Pages.

Ownership and contacts
- SLO/contract template owner: Platform & Product (primary: Marco Hernandez, secondary: Priya Singh).
- Capacity forecasting and billing correlation: Finance + Eng-SRE (lead: Lin Zhao).
- Dedicated onboarding and migration playbook: Eng Private Deployments (lead: Diego Morales).
- Observability and SLI instrumentation: Eng Platform (rt-collector, dashboard owners).

Assumptions for capacity modeling (canonical workload profile)
- Baseline request mix (median customer): 60% short chat messages (avg 40 tokens), 30% medium generations (avg 200 tokens), 10% embedding/rerank calls.
- Average tokens per request: 70 tokens.
- Average GPU throughput: 80 tokens/sec for our production quantized model variant on A100-80GB equivalent under continuous batching.
- Effective throughput after KV-cache sharing and prefix caching: +25% for chat workloads (hot prefixes).
- Operational buffer: 20% headroom for autoscaling and burst capacity.

Capacity formula (example)
- Required GPU slots = ceil( (expected_avg_qps * avg_tokens_per_request) / (tokens_per_gpu_sec * 3600) * safety_factor )
- Example: expected_avg_qps = 120 requests/sec, avg_tokens = 70, tokens_per_gpu_sec = 80 -> base_gpus = ceil((120*70)/(80)) = ceil(105) = 105 GPU-seconds equivalent; apply safety_factor 1.2 -> 126 slots (rounded per pool sizing rules).

Telemetry and billing correlation
- Implement a capacity billing metric that maps request tokens + batching efficiency to GPU-slot-seconds. This metric has to be exportable from runtime (batcher + router) and correlatable with cloud provider GPU usage.
- Key telemetry points: tokens_emitted, batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_variant_id, gpu_util_percent, gpu_slot_seconds_by_pool.
- Target: telemetry pipeline must provide end-to-end reconciliation within 5 business days of invoice start by Q2 2026.

Roadmap & milestones (high level)
1) Q4 2025 – Discovery & templates\   - Finalize SLC templates for Hosted and Dedicated.\   - Run retrospective on 2025 incident impact on capacity (see Retrospective section).
2) Q1 2026 – Instrumentation & billing prototype\   - Ship runtime exports for gpu_slot_seconds_by_pool and tokens_emitted.\   - Start pilot billing reconciliation with 3 enterprise customers.
3) Q2 2026 – SLO publication & automated alerts\   - Publish SLO dashboards and automated error-budget alerts in Grafana / Opsgenie.\   - Integrate billing telemetry into Console cost reports (token-level -> capacity mapping).
4) Q3 2026 – Dedicated guarantees and GA features\   - Ship Dedicated SLA page and contract boilerplate.\   - Improve autoscaler to honor per-tenant burst budget and pre-warm slots.
5) Q4 2026 – Cost optimization wave\   - Roll out quantization profiles per-workload class and validate output-quality regressions.\   - Target 18% unit cost reduction across median workloads.\\nDeployment phases and rollout playbook
- Phase 0 (Prep): Update service descriptor catalog with SLO tags and add contract boilerplate to legal templates.
- Phase 1 (Pilot): Enable telemetry for 3 candidate customers (mix of Hosted/Dedicated) and run two-week soak tests. Document regressions in the regression-triage page.
- Phase 2 (Controlled rollout): Open SLCs to new Dedicated customers with contractual language for capacity and burst. Use canary assignment for autoscaler changes (5% of pools).
- Phase 3 (GA): Publish public SLOs for Hosted, update Console to show per-tenant capacity burn rates and alerts.

Alerting and dashboard requirements
- SLI set (minimum): request_success_rate, p50_latency, p95_latency, p99_latency, tokens_emitted_per_minute, batch_size_avg, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_util_percent, ready_gpu_slots.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - request_success_rate drop below 99.0% for 5m -> P1 page + oncall.
  - p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for 10m -> P1 page.
  - gpu_util_percent sustained > 92% for 15m and ready_gpu_slots < 10% -> scale-up runbook.
  - batch_size_avg drops below configured baseline for 30m -> investigate router backpressure.
- Dashboards: per-region and per-pool SLO dashboard, per-model performance heatmap, capacity forecast widget (12h/72h/30d).

Runbooks and automation hooks (summary)
- Scale-up runbook (automated):
  1. Check autoscaler logs for failed provisioning events.
  2. Verify cloud provider quota and pre-warm API calls.
  3. If provisioning failed > 3 attempts, trigger manual provisioning escalation to cloud-ops (Escalation matrix id: ENG-PLAT-ESC-02).
- Degradation fallback runbook:
  1. Route new requests to compatible smaller model variant with fallback-rules in router-svc.
  2. Enable prefix-only KV cache mode to reduce memory pressure.
  3. Notify affected customers and mark incident on status page.

Risk matrix and mitigations
- Risk: Overcommit of GPU slots causes sustained saturation -> Mitigation: conservative safety_factor (default 1.2), automated headroom monitors.
- Risk: Inaccurate telemetry mapping leads to billing disputes -> Mitigation: reconciliation pilot, daily reconciliation reports during pilot.
- Risk: Latency regression after quantization -> Mitigation: auto-eval regression harness with guardrail thresholds and rollback rules.

Retrospective summary (2025 incidents & learnings)
- Incident: Nov 2025 cross-region failover resulted in 30% capacity loss in eu-west-1 due to mis-ordered autoscaler dependencies.\- Root cause: autoscaler bootstrap ordering + missing readiness probe for router-svc.\- Actions taken: 1) Added readiness dependency checks for router-svc; 2) Implemented pre-warm policy for hot pools; 3) Added capacity contingency of +15% for cross-region failover.

Operational checklist for new Dedicated customer onboarding
1. Contract & SLC signed with stated baseline GPU slots and burst policy.
2. Pre-provision Dedicated pool in staging and run 48h soak test with customer workload.
3. Enable detailed telemetry exports and share sample reconciliations.\4. Approve go-live via joint runbook rehearsal and rollback plan.

Appendices
- A. Example SLC snippet (contract appendix):
  {
    "modeling": "baseline_throughput": "10k req/min",
    "availability": "99.95%",
    "burst_policy": "2x baseline for up to 10 minutes per hour"
  }
- B. Example CLI to dump pool telemetry (runtime debug):
  ```bash
  # Query pool telemetry for the last hour\  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/pools/$POOL_ID/telemetry?from=-60m\" | jq '.metrics | {tokens_emitted, batch_size_avg, gpu_util_percent}'
  ```
